stem: For a one-unit straight task move with constant J=diag(1,0.01), no first-component motion and |qdot2|≤10, what is the fastest constant second-component speed and its travel time, compared with an intended one-second move?

options.text: Speed 0.1 and travel time 1 s; reducing speed does not affect the scheduled arrival
Speed 1 and travel time 1 s; the joint-rate limit remains satisfied
Speed 0.01 and travel time 100 s; this is the fastest permitted motion
Speed 0.1 and travel time 10 s; the geometric move is retained but its intended timing is slowed

assumptions: This is a hypothetical locally scaled example with the displayed diagonal Jacobian assumed constant over the move.
Task units are consistently scaled, joint2 rate units match the bound, and endpoint acceleration transitions are excluded.
Slowing a feasible direction does not make an infeasible direction attainable at an exact singularity.

stem: An LSPB segment starts at global time 5 s, lasts 2 s and uses blend duration 0.3 s at each end; at global times 5.2, 6.0 and 6.8 s, which local times and regions should the runtime selector use?

options.text: Local times 5.2,6.0,6.8 s: final blend at all three updates
Local times 0.2,1.0,1.8 s: linear region, initial blend, final blend
Local times 0.2,1.0,1.8 s: initial blend, final blend, linear region
Local times 0.2,1.0,1.8 s: initial blend, linear region, final blend

assumptions: Use the stated hypothetical symmetric LSPB timing; no sample lies exactly at a boundary.
This selection test does not silently correct the source’s separate blend-position/velocity inconsistency.
